-- A statement taken of a person: their due-total then (two decimals, or n/a), how many of their
-- claims counted, and the sheet's today when it was taken. A person's statements are in the order
-- of their ids; the last one is the person's last statement.
CREATE TABLE statement (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    taken_on  DATE         NOT NULL,
    due_total VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    claims    INT          NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX statement_person ON statement (person_id, id);

-- Whether the claim is bound by its person's last statement, and the due it was bound to (null when
-- it had none then: n/a). A bound claim shows and totals that due until the next statement.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN stated BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN stated_due DECIMAL(14, 2);
-- What a statement as of a date needs to see the sheet as it stood then: the sheet's today when each change was
-- made. Null on rows made before this was kept: they count as made at any date.

-- The sheet's today when the statement was taken (taken_on is the date it was taken as of).
ALTER TABLE statement ADD COLUMN made_on DATE;
-- The sheet's today when the person was added, and when their retirement was last recorded.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN added_on DATE;
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN retired_on DATE;
-- The sheet's today when the hold was added.
ALTER TABLE person_hold ADD COLUMN made_on DATE;

-- Each setting of a rate, in the order it was made, with the sheet's today then. A grade's rates as they stood at the
-- end of a date are the last settings of each from-date made on or before it.
CREATE TABLE rate_log (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(100)  NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    grade     VARCHAR(1)    NOT NULL,
    from_date DATE,
    to_date   DATE,
    pct       DECIMAL(5, 2) NOT NULL,
    set_on    DATE          NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX rate_log_sheet_grade ON rate_log (sheet_id, grade, id);
-- Where the statement stands among its person's statements: a person's statements are in the order of seq, then id,
-- and the last one is the person's last statement. Statements that follow a person merged into another are placed
-- before that person's own, so the receiving person's last statement stays theirs.
ALTER TABLE statement ADD COLUMN seq BIGINT;
UPDATE statement SET seq = id;
ALTER TABLE statement ALTER COLUMN seq SET NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX statement_person_seq ON statement (person_id, seq, id);

# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

# Refuse to run against a server that is not ours: an app left running on $PORT (an earlier
# bin/start that was never stopped, another sandbox) would take the tests and fail them all.
if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "bin/e2e: something is already serving on port ${PORT}; stop it (bin/stop) or set PORT to a free port" >&2
  exit 2
fi

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# app's REST endpoints. Returns once
# launching; poll /actuator/health for readiness.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid
# Spring Boot host config. H2 in-memory in the same JVM; Flyway migrates the schema up on boot from
# db/migration; Actuator health is the readiness probe.

# In-memory H2 (dies with the JVM = clean per-run reset).
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:officehq;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1;LOCK_TIMEOUT=10000
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=
# Pooled connections are never retired: when HikariCP closes one at its default 30 min
# max-lifetime, this in-memory H2 closes under the remaining sessions and every later statement
# fails with "The database has been closed" while the health probe stays UP. 0 means no lifetime.
spring.datasource.hikari.max-lifetime=0

# Flyway owns the schema. JPA does not create tables.
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
# Close the persistence context at the end of the request, not during view rendering.
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

# Readiness probe.
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health
management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true

# The SPA is served from src/main/resources/static (built there by bin/build); deep-link
# fallback is in SpaConfig.java.

# Audit sink: one record per line to this known file, so tests assert side-effects by reading it.
# bin/start passes an absolute path via AUDIT_FILE; default is .run/audit.log.
app.audit.file=${AUDIT_FILE:.run/audit.log}

I've added the statement lines to each person, but only 3 of the 4 tests pass as the code stands. Scenario 2 fails because of the real calendar date, not because of the new lines.

**What changed**
- **Server:** `StatementSummary.java` now keeps the person's remaining statements and turns them into lines like `2026-03-11 2.00`, sorted oldest first by statement date. Two on the same date stay in the order they were taken. `PersonController.java` sends these lines with each person as `statementLines`.
- **Cancelled and moved statements:** cancelling a statement already deletes it, so it drops off the list. A merge or transfer already moves the statements to the receiving person, so they show among that person's own, by date.
- **Front end:** `people.ts` adds a "Statement lines" column with one `data-testid="person-statement-line-line"` per line.
- No database change was needed.

**Why scenario 2 fails**
- At line 800 the test reads a claim's due while viewing the sheet as of 2026-03-20. It expects `1.29`; the app shows `n/a`.
- The cause is that a sheet the test hasn't dated yet starts on the real date (`LocalDate.now()` in `SheetService.java:207`). The test never sets a date on the parent sheet, so its rates are recorded as set on 2026-11-12. In a view as of 2026-03-20 those rates didn't exist yet, so there's no rate to fall back on.
- The expected `1.29` only comes out when the real date is on or before 2026-03-20, so the test was probably generated before then.
- To confirm, I temporarily fixed that start date at 2026-03-01: all 4 tests passed. I then put `LocalDate.now()` back.

I didn't change how dated views pick rates just to match this one test. That would change app behaviour well beyond this request, and the test can't pass on today's date without it. To get it passing, either run it with the system clock set before 2026-03-20, or regenerate the test so it sets a date on the parent sheet too.
